title: Java developer tools used in day-to-day work
answer: As a Java developer, the tools I commonly work with include IntelliJ IDEA for coding, navigation, refactoring, debugging, and Spring support; JDK tools for compiling and running Java; Maven for dependency management and build automation; Git for source control; and automated test tooling such as JUnit through the Maven build. For API development I use tools such as Postman, while database work may involve SQL clients or database IDEs depending on the platform. For delivery and operations I am familiar with CI/CD tools such as Jenkins or GitHub Actions, container tooling such as Docker, and deployment platforms such as Kubernetes when the project requires them. I also use logs, metrics, profilers, and command-line diagnostics during troubleshooting. The exact tool set depends on the project, but I prefer a reproducible workflow where the IDE, build, source control, tests, and CI all agree on the same project configuration.

steps.title: Start with IntelliJ IDEA
steps.question: A Java developer's tool set should support the whole coding cycle rather than only text editing. Why is IntelliJ IDEA useful for navigation, refactoring, inspections, debugging, and Spring-aware development in one workspace?
steps.why: IntelliJ gives the project one place for source navigation, typed refactoring, inspections, debugging, framework awareness, build integration, and terminal access.
steps.why_te: IntelliJ source navigation, typed refactoring, inspections, debugging, Spring awareness, build integration mariyu terminal access ni oka workspace lo istundi. Anduke Java development lo IDE central tool ga useful.

steps.title: Inspect the configured JDK
steps.question: The IDE is only one part of the environment; Java itself is provided by the JDK. Why should a Java developer treat the configured JDK as a core development tool rather than an invisible machine dependency?
steps.why: The JDK controls the compiler, runtime, language level, diagnostics, and many command-line utilities, so its version directly affects what the project can build and run.
steps.why_te: JDK compiler, runtime, language level, diagnostics mariyu command-line utilities ni provide chestundi. Daani version project build mariyu run behavior ni direct ga affect chestundi kabatti idi core development tool.

steps.title: Use Maven for the build
steps.question: Enterprise Java projects depend on many libraries and repeatable lifecycle tasks. Why is Maven a core tool for dependency management, compilation, testing, and packaging instead of leaving those tasks to IDE-specific buttons?
steps.why: Maven makes the build portable and repeatable outside IntelliJ, which is essential for teammates and CI systems.
steps.why_te: Maven build ni IntelliJ ki matrame depend kakunda portable mariyu repeatable ga chestundi. Dependencies, compile, test, package lifecycle teammates mariyu CI lo kuda same ga run avutayi.

steps.title: Use Git for source control
steps.question: Java development is collaborative and every production change needs traceability. What role does Git play beyond simply keeping a backup of source files?
steps.why: Git records change history, supports branches and diffs, and provides the basis for code review, collaboration, rollback, and CI triggers.
steps.why_te: Git source backup matrame kaadu. Change history, branches, diffs, collaboration, code review, rollback mariyu CI triggers ki base ga work chestundi.

steps.title: Inspect Spring-aware tooling
steps.question: A Spring Boot application contains framework concepts that are not obvious from individual Java files. Why is Spring-aware IDE tooling useful when working with beans, mappings, properties, and application lifecycle?
steps.why: Framework-aware tooling helps connect source code to the runtime concepts Spring creates around it, reducing the effort needed to navigate a large application.
steps.why_te: Spring-aware tooling Java source ni beans, mappings, properties mariyu application lifecycle tho connect chestundi. Large application lo framework relationships ni fast ga understand cheyyadaniki idi help chestundi.

steps.title: Use the integrated terminal
steps.question: A graphical IDE does not replace command-line verification. Why should Java developers remain comfortable running build, Git, runtime, and diagnostic commands from a terminal?
steps.why: Direct command execution exposes the real tools used by CI and production troubleshooting and makes environment problems easier to diagnose.
steps.why_te: Terminal nundi direct commands run chesthe CI use chese real tools tho same behavior verify cheyyachu. Environment, build mariyu troubleshooting problems ni diagnose cheyyadam kuda easy avutundi.

steps.title: Check Java from the terminal
steps.question: When several JDKs are installed, IDE configuration and shell PATH can disagree. What does checking `java --version` tell you about the actual Java tool being used in the current terminal?
steps.why: It confirms the runtime executable that commands will use, preventing version drift from being mistaken for a source-code problem.
steps.why_te: `java --version` current terminal actual ga ye Java runtime use chestundo confirm chestundi. Version drift ni source-code issue laga confuse avvakunda help chestundi.

steps.title: Check Maven from the terminal
steps.question: The Maven tool window is convenient, but the command-line build is what CI commonly executes. Why is `mvn -version` a useful toolchain check for a Java developer?
steps.why: It verifies both Maven and the Java runtime Maven is using, which helps expose local build-tool mismatches early.
steps.why_te: `mvn -version` Maven version mariyu Maven use chestunna Java runtime renditini chupistundi. Local build-tool mismatch ni mundhe identify cheyyadaniki idi useful.

steps.title: Check Git from the terminal
steps.question: Source control operations may be performed through IntelliJ or from the command line. Why is checking `git --version` useful when describing a reproducible Java development tool set?
steps.why: It proves the underlying Git client is present independently of the IDE integration, which matters for scripts, hooks, and CI-style workflows.
steps.why_te: `git --version` underlying Git client IDE integration ki separate ga available undani confirm chestundi. Scripts, hooks mariyu CI-style workflows lo idi important.

steps.title: Finish with automated verification
steps.question: A long list of tools is not valuable unless they work together consistently. Why should a Java developer prove the environment with the project's automated test command before considering the toolchain ready?
steps.why: The test gate exercises the JDK, Maven build, dependencies, compiled code, and test framework together and therefore provides evidence that the development toolchain is coherent.
steps.why_te: Automated test gate JDK, Maven build, dependencies, compiled code mariyu test framework anni kalisi correct ga work chestunnayi ani prove chestundi. Tool list kanna ee reproducible verification mukhyam.
